issue: No official market prices exist. nfl.com publishes no spreads, totals or moneylines, so every market column is left blank.
why_it_matters: Closing line value, ROI and any against-the-spread record cannot be computed. The -110 figures are a flat-price scenario, not a record against real closing lines.

issue: Jacoby Brissett is listed as Baltimore's first-string quarterback on baltimoreravens.com, while an official nfl.com news item reports Arizona benched him in Week 8.
why_it_matters: Two clubs' ratings and every line touching either of them depend on which club he actually plays for.

issue: Daiyan Henley appears on the Los Angeles Chargers' official Week 10 injury report, while an official nfl.com news item reports Denver traded for him on 10 November 2026.
why_it_matters: Injury data could be attributed to the wrong club.

issue: No power calculation is published for the home-field advantage estimate.
why_it_matters: A power calculation would require assuming a per-game variance that is itself unmeasured; publishing one would be an inference.

issue: Eight games are labelled neutral-site from the official schedule pages; the venue of each has not been independently re-confirmed.
why_it_matters: Home-field advantage is zeroed for these games, so a wrong label misprices that game.

issue: No official player-statistic source was in scope, so no player-prop correlation is published.
why_it_matters: The prop-bet and prop-parlay parts of the brief cannot be started. The official stats site was not fetched this session.

issue: The out-of-sample record is 89 bets drawn from a single partial season.
why_it_matters: Every hit rate carries a wide interval; treating any of them as established is not supportable.

issue: The totals model's bias is measured but not corrected, and the model is fitted on one partial season only.
why_it_matters: Published totals may be systematically off in one direction.

issue: Houston: houstontexans.com publishes its depth chart as an image with no machine-readable rows
why_it_matters: Backup and deficiency tracking cannot be verified for this club, so its rows are blank rather than guessed

issue: packers.com stamps its depth chart 'Unofficial' and does not list Micah Parsons, although he appears as limited on the official injury report.
why_it_matters: Green Bay's defensive deficiency index may be understated.

issue: miamidolphins.com lists a single quarterback, Kyle McCord, and no backup, after Malik Willis was reported placed on injured reserve.
why_it_matters: Miami's offensive deficiency beyond the first string is undefined; no value is filled in.

issue: The 2026 NFL rulebook was not retrieved, so no 2026 rule change is reflected in the model.
why_it_matters: Scoring, overtime and extra-point rules affect totals and margin distributions.

issue: Signals are tested at a flat -110 price on both sides regardless of how large a favourite the model picks.
why_it_matters: In reality a big favourite is not priced at -110, so the flat-price record overstates what would actually have been bettable.

issue: Two candidate signals (backing a post-bye club, and backing a club with a rest edge of 3 or more days) were discovered AFTER scanning the correlation table, not declared in advance, and rest on 14 and 26 graded games respectively.
why_it_matters: Post-hoc signals found by scanning many correlations are exactly the situation the deflated Sharpe ratio exists to penalise. Both fail the minimum-sample gate and the deflation gate.

issue: philadelphiaeagles.com labels its depth chart UNOFFICIAL - compiled by the Eagles Communications Department - and publishes one defensive-tackle row with no first-string player at all.
why_it_matters: Philadelphia's depth is a club estimate rather than an official chart, and one position has no published starter.

issue: data/standings-2026-wk8.csv abbreviates Arizona as AZ. nfl.com publishes ARI, and this repository's own data/teams.csv uses ARI.
why_it_matters: A non-official team code silently breaks any join between that table and official data, or between it and the rest of the repo.

issue: data/model_lines_2026_wk9.csv builds its Week 9 lines on a home-field advantage of +2.0 points, described in the file as the 2002-2024 mean home margin. This season's own games measure +0.47 points, with a 95% interval of -1.81 to +2.75 that contains zero.
why_it_matters: Every Week 9 line built on that input is shifted about two points toward the home team, in a season whose data does not support any home-field advantage at all.

issue: Seven existing data files carry numbers this session could not re-verify from an official source: player passing statistics, the 2025 results file, historical base rates, the three correlation files and the league-facts file.
why_it_matters: Those numbers are currently treated as verified in the repository, but nothing in this session's official sources confirms them.
source_or_action: See repo-audit.html for the per-file list and the reason each one was left unchecked
